body: I will try to reproduce this on 10.10 later tonight.

Yep, I can reproduce this on 10.10 with `./tests/events` executable (it uses `glfwWaitEvents()` in its main loop) on latest `master` (6743761c2).

The window has to be focused and the mouse cursor has to be over it, then the CPU usage goes from 0.0%-0.6% to 40-60% (with `WindowServer` process taking up the remaining CPU time, they add up to 100%).

Let me try some older versions, like 3.0.4, and see if it happens there too.

**Edit:** It does not happen with 3.0.4, cpu usage is around 2.4% at most with that version. So this is clearly a regression. Likely related to one of the cursor-related bugfixes. :( Alternatively, it might be related to `glfwPostEmptyEvent()`?

I'm able to reproduce this as well with the sample app from the documentation page. Even worse, when the window is _not_ focussed, CPU usage jumps to 60-70% because the frame rate limit of 60 fps is not respected.

issue.body:
Running this on OS X (10.10) is a lot slower than it used to be. It seems like GLFW had some upstream regressions, as most of the time is spent in `glfwPlatformWaitEvents()`.

![ld2tf](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/52399/5279269/1f54d46e-7ae3-11e4-93e6-be89844433f4.png)

body: I can confirm that 1ccc23268cfb5217c91b64eb44dfb77ad3c4fc7e does not have this issue.

After some further debugging, it turned out that our speed issue was solely related to changing the window title on every frame triggered these updates. Like @zhanggyb, I saw very high CPU usage in glfwWaitEvents(). After removing the title update, this is gone. Note that this behavior _did not exist_ in 1ccc23268cfb5217c91b64eb44dfb77ad3c4fc7e; while updating the title isn't super fast in that revision either, it certainly is a lot faster and uses less CPU than the current master.

But I was able to reproduce the problem in `./tests/events`, and its code doesn't seem to be setting the window title every frame?

https://github.com/glfw/glfw/blob/e1ae9af5a08f283a7edc2c0c59738a8da66a8074/tests/events.c

Could someone verify whether [this branch](https://github.com/glfw/glfw/tree/cursorfixes) fixes this issue? I'm finishing up 3.1 and don't want to risk 10.10 breaking anything right now.

Ping @shurcooL.
I will do that this evening!

All seems well in the cursorfixes branch. Tried tests/events on 10.10.1 as someone mentioned the problem is reproducible with it but CPU usage stayed at 0.2% when idling and below a few % with input.

EDIT: someone else please verify this as well.
